**In one line**: Two newspapers have reportedly filed suit against OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming their articles were used to train AI models without consent.

### Key points
- Two newspapers are reported to have sued OpenAI and Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement.
- The core dispute is whether their articles were used to train generative AI without permission or compensation.
- The case echoes earlier lawsuits from outlets such as The New York Times.

### Why it matters
Copyright disputes between news publishers and AI companies are hardening from isolated cases into a broad trend. The outcomes could directly shape licensing costs for AI training data and how publishers are compensated.
